title: How to use Graph Data in the Wild to Help Graph Anomaly Detection?

problem.claim: Graph anomaly detection is challenged by scarce labels, ill-defined anomalies, varying anomaly types, and difficulty accurately capturing the normal distribution when data is insufficient.

gap.claim: Existing unsupervised approaches may be limited because insufficient data makes accurate and comprehensive modeling of the normal distribution difficult.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Wild-GAD, a framework that uses external graph data to help graph anomaly detection tasks.
Wild-GAD is built on UniWildGraph, a unified database containing diverse graph data with broad domain coverage, ample volume, and a unified feature space.
The framework uses selection criteria based on representativity and diversity to identify suitable external data for each anomaly detection task.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Wild-GAD as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on six real-world test datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of Wild-GAD.
The authors report average improvements of 18% in AUCROC and 32% in AUCPR over the best-competing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph anomaly detection has applications across social, financial, and communication networks.
Graph anomalies pose challenges for supervised and semi-supervised methods, while insufficient data limits unsupervised modeling of normal distributions.
The paper proposes using external graph data and introduces the Wild-GAD framework.
Wild-GAD uses the UniWildGraph database and representativity- and diversity-based selection criteria.
Experiments on six real-world datasets report effectiveness and average AUCROC and AUCPR improvements over competing methods.

source_observation.claim: External graph data is selected using representativity and diversity criteria for each anomaly detection task.

interpretation.claim: When task-specific data is insufficient, carefully selected external data may provide useful supplementary information.

application.claim: Consider augmenting graph anomaly detection with external graph data selected for task relevance and diversity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when external data selection fails or how selection criteria behave across different tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the model architecture or training procedure.
The abstract does not identify the six datasets, baselines, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide uncertainty estimates or per-dataset results.
